note: The slider starts at 1854, the year the town was laid out, then uses the census years from 1860 through 2020. 1854 was not a census year. No 1860 population for the town was found. Firms from the 1885 history are listed under 1880, and January 1886 Sanborn labels are listed under 1890. Each line keeps its own source year.

census.text: No population count was found. There was no census in 1854. The town was laid out this year, before the railroad was finished. The first public sale of lots was in May 1854: about 70 lots, about $6,000, priced from $30 to $120.
census.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter

school.text: No data found. No school is named in the year the town was laid out. The first schoolhouse came in 1856.
school.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter

businesses.name: Hiram and Daniel Markham
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: They opened in the summer of 1854 in a small slab store. The centennial book places it on the northeast corner of East Main and Wells. The 1885 history says it stood on the later normal-college site. That second site was not located, so the store is drawn on the centennial corner.

census.text: No data found for a population. Bushnell was not yet a city (the charter came in 1869), and Bushnell Township was not set off until 1866, from the south half of Prairie City Township. No 1860 count for the town was found.
census.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell Township chapter, for the 1866 division. The city charter date is the one already used for this town.

census.text: By the close of 1856 the history counts 125 buildings on the town site, including houses, stables, and barns. Their lots were not given, so those lots stay empty.
census.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter

school.text: No enrollment count was found. The first schoolhouse was built in 1856 on Sperry Street, block 57, and Dan Markham was the first teacher. In 1860 the school was moved to Temperance hall, later the Normal eating house. That hall was not located on a lot, so it is not drawn.
school.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter

businesses.name: James Cole
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: He opened in December 1855 in a one-story frame store, 16 by 48 feet, brought from Quincy, on the later site of T. F. Seibert's store. The building was afterward moved to New Philadelphia. The year it left, and Seibert's corner, were not found, so that first store is not drawn.

businesses.name: Wilson & Co.
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: S. A. Hendee joined this firm in April 1860, on the east side of the railroad. The door was not named. The brick corner at Hurst and West Main is a later building, so it is not drawn in 1860.

businesses.name: Miller & Krouser
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: The first furniture store, about 1859, a little east of the Bushnell House. That hotel's lot is itself inferred, so this store is not given a door.

businesses.name: E. P. Kinney & Co.
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: The first store kept for hardware alone, opened in 1857. The centennial list spells the name Kline. The lot was not found. No data found for whether the firm was still open in 1860.

businesses.name: Markham's store building
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: Hiram Markham built it after the slab store, where Ball and Son later had the carriage shop, East Main at Gridley. Negley and Angle opened there in April 1856. Who kept the store in 1860 was not found.

census.text: The Toledo, Peoria and Warsaw is shown from this stop. A railroad chronology records that it opened between La Harpe and Bushnell on January 1, 1868. The 1885 history says the line was surveyed through town in 1867.
census.source: Christopher T. Baer, Pennsylvania Railroad chronology, 1868. 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter.

school.text: A graded school was established in 1868. Mr. Hyde was the first principal. No enrollment count for 1870 was found.
school.source: Arthur Loomis, 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter. The date he gives is 1868.

school.text: From 1868 until the 1875 building, the history says there were four schools, one in each ward. The 1875 schoolhouse is not drawn in 1870. No enrollment count for 1870 was found.
school.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter

businesses.name: S. A. Hendee
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: In trade on the east side of the railroad from April 1860. By 1870 he was operating the store alone, after Hendee and Clarke dissolved in the fall of 1867. The West Main brick corner is not dated, so it is not drawn in 1870.

businesses.name: James Cole
businesses.source: Bushnell centennial book, 1854–1954
businesses.note: His brick corner at East Main and Hail uses bricks he made in the 1860s. The exact year was not found. He was still a merchant. Banking came in 1878.

businesses.name: Nevius Brothers
businesses.source: Bushnell centennial book, 1854–1954
businesses.note: Listed as the first flouring mill. The 1885 history calls the Nevious Bros. mill the Excelsior. The Depot Mill's date was not found.

businesses.name: West & Kaiser
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: The stand opened in March 1866 as a general store on the east side of the street. Stockton West came in, and by the fall of 1869 the firm was West and Kaiser, in a new room. Neither door was named.

businesses.name: Lemuel Aller
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: Began in 1867 as J. H. Aller and Co., and bought his partner's interest in the fall of 1869. The door was not named.

businesses.name: Aller, Seibert & Co.
businesses.source: 1885 History of McDonough County, Bushnell chapter
businesses.note: Theodore F. Seibert's store was established in March 1870 by this firm. The corner was not named, so it is not drawn.

school.text: No count of children enrolled in 1880, or in 1886, was found.
school.source: The 1885 county history describes the building and does not give a pupil count. Illinois superintendent reports for 1884–1886 were not found in a form that could be read.

school.text: Public school described in 1885: eight classrooms (rooms 3 through 10), a superintendent’s room, and a two-room primary building on the north side. John P. Yoder had been superintendent since 1880. Teachers, fuel, and the like cost about $600 a month.
school.source: Arthur Loomis, 1885 History of McDonough County. This is not a headcount.

school.text: The 1875–76 building is also described as eight classrooms and four basement rooms. The first high-school class, in 1878, was 6 graduates (one boy and five girls).
school.source: Bushnell centennial book, 1854–1954. The class year is 1878.

school.text: Western Normal College opened July 20, 1881, with about 15 pupils, about 20 before the term ended, and about 300 different students before that first year closed.
school.source: Bushnell centennial book. These are 1881 figures, not an 1880 or 1886 public-school enrollment. The January 1886 Sanborn map still labels the building Western Normal School. The same book says the school later closed and was revived in 1888.

school.text: In October 1900, Superintendent of Schools W. H. Miller was told that students from the local high school would be admitted to the University of Illinois without examination. No enrollment count was found.
The 1875–76 brick school burned in 1896. A replacement was built in about nine months. No enrollment count was found.
school.source: Bushnell centennial book, 1854–1954. The fire year is 1896.

school.text: In February 1903 voters approved a new school on the east side. The East Side school opened in the winter of 1904, before Christmas, as a grade and high school. No enrollment count was found.

census.text: The 1918 Good Hope sheet draws the streets past the 1854 plat, including the south leg of Cole Street to the section-line road. A compiled list dates Illinois 9 and Illinois 41 to 1918; the sheet itself does not print the numbers. The same sheet's black building squares within three miles are drawn from this stop, a house for an isolated square and a barn when a second square sits in the same yard. Rural roads that the sheet already shows, and that the 1974 quadrangle prints in red, are drawn too. No family name is printed on the quadrangle. Five country schools named on this sheet are drawn as small frame schoolhouses: Maple Grove, School No. 5, Birds, Possum Hollow, and Railroad. Each sits on the building square nearest its printed name. That placement is an estimate.
census.source: U.S. Geological Survey, Good Hope, Illinois, 15-minute quadrangle, 1918. OpenStreetMap centerlines matched to that sheet.

U.S. decennial census, city of Bushnell, McDonough County, Illinois. 1870 (2,003) and 1880 (2,316) are the counts already used for this town. 1890 (2,314) is also the figure a Rand McNally atlas printed in 1895. 1900 (2,490) is also printed in the Historical Encyclopedia of Illinois (1907). Later decades are the same census series, as compiled in the historical population table for the city.

census.text: Hiel Drive, the loop north of West Main, is shown from this stop. The assessor dates 10 Hiel Drive to 1951, the earliest house in Hiel Subdivision. The 1918 Good Hope sheet does not draw the loop. Lakelawn Estate stays off this stop: its earliest structure year is 1963. No tornado was found in McDonough County for 1968, and 1969 has no tornado in the same record, so no trees are taken out for one.

census.text: Lakelawn Estate, with its pond, is drawn southeast of town: Hillcrest Drive, Lakeview Drive, Sunrise Lane, and Sunset Lane. The assessor dates its houses from 1963 (21 Hillcrest Drive) through 1979. West Hess is drawn from this stop. Washington Court is not on these sheets. Red rural roads that the 1974 sheets print, and that the 1918 and 1944 sheets do not, are drawn from this stop.
